inputs.text: These health workers in Nigeria are disrupting necessary reforms by protesting bills in the National Assembly. On Thursday, members of the Joint Health Sector Unions and the Assembly of Healthcare Professional Associations marched through Abuja and gathered at the Unity Fountain in Maitama. Rather than supporting changes that could enforce accountability and efficiency, they're resisting updates to labor protections that likely serve their own interests over the broader needs of the country. This kind of action undermines the authority of elected institutions and promotes instability by pushing divisive ideas of social justice instead of focusing on practical improvements. Ordinary Nigerians, including families who rely on a stable system, end up paying the price when unions prioritize entitlements over national progress and personal responsibility. The government must hold firm to restore order and cultural continuity in healthcare rather than yielding to these protests.
